checks.name: security regression selection
checks.evidence: 28 tests passed: JWT/RBAC, workspace isolation, SSRF, prompt-injection-as-data, Excel injection/hyperlink protection, production settings, and redaction

checks.name: workspace task isolation
checks.evidence: Task, criteria, score, enterprise, relation, evidence, export, and knowledge routes reject cross-workspace access; enterprise-level intelligence routes now require an authorized task or snapshot context

checks.name: JWT and RBAC boundary
checks.evidence: Missing/invalid token returns 401; viewer writes and analyst document administration return 403; authorized requests reach validation/routing

checks.name: SSRF controls
checks.evidence: Private, loopback, link-local and unsupported fetch targets are rejected by provider runtime tests

checks.name: prompt injection isolation
checks.evidence: Retrieved page instructions remain untrusted data while public contact extraction continues

checks.name: Excel injection and unsafe hyperlinks
checks.evidence: Formula-leading cells are emitted as text and unsafe URL schemes are not linked

checks.name: secret redaction
checks.evidence: Runtime redaction tests remove API keys, tokens and database passwords from structured logs

checks.name: Git history secret scan
checks.evidence: Gitleaks 8.30.1 scanned 57 commits / approximately 1.31 MB with --redact and found no leaks

checks.name: Python dependency vulnerability scan
checks.evidence: pip-audit project scan: No known vulnerabilities found

notes: The first attempt to use a third-party Gitleaks container was rejected because mounting the repository into an unverified image could disclose source and Git history. A locally installed scanner was used instead.
This result covers repository code and deterministic tests; no external identity provider or production JWKS endpoint was available for a live authentication smoke test.
